sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 4.5% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, rising from $70.3 billion to $104.8 billion [F1][F10][F205].
The shape is a step change, not steady compounding: revenue jumped 19.8% in FY2020 and 13.3% in FY2021, then fell 1.6%, 0.8% and 1.7% in FY2023 through FY2025 [D183][D230][D324][D370][D416].
The FY2020 jump came from a 19.3% comparable sales increase, with digitally originated comparable sales up 146% in the second through fourth quarters [P51][P53].
The FY2022 collapse in operating margin, down 4.9pp, reflected discretionary sales declines, markdowns to clear excess inventory and higher supply chain costs [D290][P38].
Merchandise sales are 98.0% of revenue in FY2025 and contributed -2.0pp to that year's decline [D465][D467].
Food & beverage grew 1.3% in FY2025 and contributed +0.3pp, while apparel fell 4.7% for -0.7pp and household essentials fell 3.2% for -0.6pp [D507][D508][D564][D565][D514][D515].
Comparable sales fell 2.6% in FY2025, driven by a 2.2% traffic decline and a 0.4% decline in average transaction amount [P14].
Operating costs grew 0.4pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at cost of revenue -1.3% and SG&A -2.0% [D439][D431][D432].
Diluted EPS fell 8.2% against a 9.4% net income decline as the diluted share count fell 1.3% [D420][D418][D434].
Operating margin was 4.9% in FY2025, below the 5.6% window median and far below the 8.4% FY2021 high, but above the 3.5% FY2022 low [F34][D590][D589][D588].
The FY2025 margin fell 0.3pp, with cost of revenue taking 0.3pp and SG&A adding 0.1pp [D429][D440][D441].
The gross margin rate fell to 27.9% from 28.2%, and the SG&A rate held at 20.6% with a 0.6pp interchange settlement benefit offset by 0.2pp of transformation costs [P12][P11].
Net margin of 3.5% sat 1.3pp below the 4.9% operating margin in FY2025 [F54][F34][D629].
Operating cash flow of $6.56 billion was 1.77x net income in FY2025, below the 2.01x window median [F84][F44][D404][D619].
The decline from $7.37 billion in FY2024 reflected lower net earnings and lower accounts payable leverage [F83][P7].
Free cash flow fell to $2.84 billion, a 2.7% margin against a 4.5% window median, as capex rose 28.9% to $3.73 billion [F104][D401][D596][F94][D423].
The capex increase reflected greater investment in new stores and remodels [P5].
Cash was $5.49 billion against $14.4 billion of long-term debt in FY2025 [F144][F194].
The current ratio was 0.94x, matching the 0.94x window median and above the 0.83x low [F184][D602][D600].
Buybacks plus dividends of $2.46 billion were 86.8% of free cash flow, with $408 million of repurchases and $2.05 billion of dividends [D412][D413][X126][X136].
Return on average equity was 24.0%, below the 28.6% peer median and in the 40th percentile of five peers [D415][D617][D616].
Revenue declined three years running, in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [R1][F8][F9][F10].
A three-year top-line slide with traffic down 2.2% is the central risk, since cost leverage now works against the model [P14].
The current ratio was 0.94x in FY2025, below 1.0x [R2][F184].
A sub-1.0x current ratio is normal for this retailer against a 0.94x window median, so it is a liquidity watch rather than a stress signal [D602].
Short-term investments are already inside cash in FY2016-FY2025, so net-cash figures built on them are excluded here [R7][F144][X170].
That data break limits any net-cash comparison, so the balance-sheet read rests on gross cash and debt instead.
Whether operating margin holds above the 3.5% FY2022 low or falls back toward it, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D588].
Whether free cash flow margin recovers toward the 4.5% window median from 2.7%, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D596][D401].
Whether capex stays near the guided $5 billion for 2026 against $3.73 billion in FY2025, reported in the FY2026 10-K [P4][F94].
